b2-integracion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rule for Changing the Tariff
b2-integracion-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Mercosur, and she asks when the common tariff can change.
b2-integracion-01.prompt: Tell Meg when the common tariff can change.
cues: Say that the tariff does not change
Say what all the partners have to do first
b2-integracion-01.target: El arancel común no cambia a menos que todos los socios estén de acuerdo.
b2-integracion-01.english: The common tariff does not change unless all the partners agree.
b2-integracion-01.canDo: I can state a condition with *siempre que*, *con tal de que* or *a menos que*.

b2-integracion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Day in Lima
b2-integracion-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Pacific Alliance, and he asks what you would have liked to see.
b2-integracion-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would have seen on 28 April 2011.
cues: Say where you would have been
Say what you would have seen
b2-integracion-02.target: Hubiera estado en Lima el 28 de abril de 2011, habría visto la firma de la Declaración de Lima.
b2-integracion-02.english: Had I been in Lima on 28 April 2011, I would have seen the signing of the Lima Declaration.
b2-integracion-02.canDo: I can say what would have happened in a past situation, with *hubiera* + past participle and no *si*.

b2-integracion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Very Deep Port
b2-integracion-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the port of Chancay, and she asks why it matters.
b2-integracion-03.prompt: Tell Meg what is special about the depth of the port.
cues: Say that the port is deep
b2-integracion-03.target: El puerto de Chancay es tan profundo que recibe barcos muy grandes.
b2-integracion-03.english: The port of Chancay is so deep that it receives very large ships.
b2-integracion-03.canDo: I can say how much of something led to a result, with *tan … que*, *tanto … que* and *de tal manera que*.

b2-integracion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Paraguay's Share of Itaipú
b2-integracion-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the Itaipú power station, and he asks what happens when Paraguay uses more electricity.
b2-integracion-04.prompt: Tell Carlos how the surplus changes as Paraguay's consumption grows.
cues: Say what happens to the surplus
b2-integracion-04.target: A medida que crece el consumo de Paraguay, queda menos excedente para vender a Brasil.
b2-integracion-04.english: As Paraguay's consumption grows, less surplus is left to sell to Brazil.
b2-integracion-04.canDo: I can describe two changes that grow together, with *a medida que* and *cuanto más … más …*.

b2-integracion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Degrees Across Borders
b2-integracion-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about the Residence Agreement, and she asks what you think should happen with university degrees.
b2-integracion-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you think the countries should do about degrees.
cues: Say what the countries should recognise
b2-integracion-05.target: Es importante que los países reconozcan los títulos universitarios de otros países.
b2-integracion-05.english: It is important that countries recognise university degrees from other countries.
b2-integracion-05.canDo: I can say what should happen, with *es importante que* and other value judgments + subjunctive.

b2-integracion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Integration Matters
b2-integracion-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about the lessons on South American integration, and he asks for one condition for the agreements to work.
b2-integracion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos one condition for the agreements to work.
cues: Say what everyone has to do
b2-integracion-consolidation.target: El acuerdo funcionará siempre que todos sigan las reglas.
b2-integracion-consolidation.english: The agreement will work as long as everyone follows the rules.
b2-integracion-consolidation.canDo: I can use conditions, past conditions, results and value judgments to talk about South American integration.
